_comment: LOCAL ground truth for the beagle import validation (scripts/populate_from_beagle.py). The fixture's sample and patient ids are real beagle identifiers, so this file is git-ignored (see .gitignore). Copy this example to .beagle_ground_truth.json and fill in the real values.
_comment_canonical: Basenames of the beagle fixtures (sample.tsv + request.tsv) loaded by the argos scenario, read from fixtures_dir.
_comment_pairs: primary_id -> [normal_id, why] for pairs beagle produces (ARGOS logic).
_comment_unpaired: primary_id -> why the normal should stay unpaired.
_comment_dmp_fixture: Path to the beagle DMP fixture (DMP_data.json with sampleStructure + patient rows).
_comment_dmp_pairs: DMP tumor primary id -> [DMP normal primary id, why]; for fixtures that DO contain a DMP T+N pair with the same patient__dmp + gene_panel (pairing runs under the DMP logic).
_comment_dmp_unpaired: DMP tumor primary id -> why the tumor stays unpaired (no same-patient__dmp same-gene_panel counterpart in the fixture).
_comment_dmp_checks: One entry per DMP record to spot-check: [sample, expected patient__cmo, expected gene_panel, expected tumor_or_normal, expected patient__dmp, expected anon_id]. Completeness of the stored record (columns + full additional_metadata) is checked automatically for every DMP sample.

expected_dmp_unpaired.<DMP tumor primary id>: no same-patient__dmp same-gene_panel counterpart in fixture
